items.title: From LaTeX to Typst
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I've been using LaTeX to generate PDF documents for a long time. I like the way LaTeX does typography and layout. Its output looks "correct" to me. That's probably because LaTeX tries hard to do the right thing. I've never seen output from a word processor that looks nearly as good.

I don't write raw LaTeX. I use it as a device for converting Org mode or Markdown files to PDF, usually via Pandoc.. I've built a complex workflow around it. Scripts, templates, boilerplate, etc. It works well. It's also wildly complicated. And so, enter Typst.

People have been mentioning Typst as a modern LaTeX alternative. I ignored it because I'd already solved the problem. It turns out that dismissing Typst as "LaTeX for Losers" was a mistake. I finally gave it a go, and found that it's similar to LaTeX, but without the steep learning curve, complexity, or multi-gigabyte download. The output is slightly different, but still looks great.

I've updated my scripts and various utilities to use Typst. It's open source, distributed as a single binary. And it's so fast!

There's some residual guilt for leaving LaTeX after so many years. I think it'll be OK without me.

items.title: Thursday, November 26, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: Here's something I don't like admitting: When I search with some non-AI search engine (e.g. StartPage or DDG), I'm like, "Ugh! I don't want to dig through all this. Just give me the answer. Like Google does!" I hate this.

items.title: Wednesday, November 25, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: I can't believe how much time I've spent, again, changing my photography workflow. I'd write a whole post about it, but it's embarrassing and I'm exhausted by it. TL;DR is that after spending days organizing and moving my library into Lightroom Classic, I'm back in Capture One sessions. You'd be exhausted too.

items.title: Kodak SlideTag
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
I'm a sucker for inexpensive little gadgets, so I impulse ordered two of the new Kodak SlideTags.

It's a tiny 6-color eink screen with a companion app for setting the displayed photo. It doesn't have to be photos. There are things like a calendar, my todo list, a name badge, qr code, etc.

They're only come as a "blind box" so you can't choose which one you want. I ordered two because I wanted to make sure I got one that said Kodachrome on it. Nope, got two if these stupid red ones. Otherwise, it's a really fun little eink device.

Oh, and it also works with Apple's Find My as an Airtag device. Neat.

items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: I don't know what to publish where, or if I want to publish anything at all. It would be easier if there was a single place to write, but easy is boring.

items.title: A note from CachyOS
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: Sunday is my day to do system maintenance. For the past month or so I've been skipping the Linux machines because I stopped thinking about Linux. This morning I'm thinking about Linux, so I'm writing this on the Beelink while I wait for like 40,000 system updates to install. Next, the ThinkPad and Framework.

items.title: Friday, November 20, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: When the Fujifilm X100VI was first announced, I preordered one that day. After waiting 6 months for one to become available, I canceled the order and moved on. That was more than two years ago, and I still want one. They are still difficult to find at retail prices, but I got a notification this morning that a black one was in stock at B&H so I dropped everything and hit that "Add to Cart" button as quickly as I could. It shipped this afternoon and will be here by Tuesday. I'll hang on to the Q2 for now, but the idea is that the Fuji will take over for the Leica as a carry-everwhere camera. It's better suited to it.

items.title: Thursday, November 19, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: I've been trying to sort of free write every day. Just one hand-written page. Then I tear it off and throw it away. It's kind of liberating.

items.title: Songs from the Second Floor (2000) ★★★★★
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: I knew nothing about Roy Andersson before watching ‎Songs from the Second Floor (2000). Now he's my current favorite filmmaker. What a bleak, funny, original, totally unique world he's made here.

items.title: Wednesday, November 18, 2026
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content:
Everything in the world is written in Markdown and I'm still using Org mode files. Contrarian much?

Oh good, The Internet is weighing in on the new Bond pick. Of course they all hate it, for all sorts of "reasons." Just like always. In a few years they'll all be saying, "See! I told you he was a great pick!"

items.title: Beyond the Valley of the Dolls (1970) ★★★★
items.author: Jack Baty
items.content: It's a miracle that this movie even exists. It makes me happy every time I watch it. I can't get over the fact that Roger Ebert wrote the screenplay and that it includes lines like, "Ere this night does wane, you will drink the black sperm of my vengeance!" So fun.
